subject: Chemistry
description: Halogens (F, Cl, Br, I, At) — Group 17, properties trends, common compounds (HCl, NaCl, ClO⁻), uses, hazards, displacement reactions.

questions.stem: Which is the most REACTIVE halogen?
questions.explanation: FLUORINE (F, atomic no. 9) — the MOST REACTIVE halogen and most electronegative element on the periodic table. WHY: smallest atomic radius → strongest pull on bonding electrons. REACTIVITY ORDER (decreasing): F > Cl > Br > I > At. STATES: F₂ — pale yellow gas; Cl₂ — yellow-green gas; Br₂ — red-brown LIQUID; I₂ — purple-black SOLID. EXTREME REACTIVITY of F₂: (a) Reacts with NEARLY ALL elements (including noble gases like Xe — to form XeF₂, XeF₄, XeF₆!). (b) Reacts EXPLOSIVELY with H₂ even in dark/cold. (c) Reacts with WATER → HF + O₂ (vigorous). (d) Reacts with GLASS (SiO₂) — must be stored in nickel/Teflon containers. KEY F COMPOUNDS: (1) HF (hydrofluoric acid) — etches glass; weak acid (only partially dissociated) but extremely corrosive to skin. (2) NaF — added to drinking water (~1 ppm) to prevent dental caries. (3) Teflon (PTFE) — non-stick polymer. (4) UF₆ — uranium-235 enrichment for nuclear fuel. (5) HFCs — refrigerants. ELECTRONEGATIVITY (Pauling scale): F = 4.0 (highest), O = 3.5, N = 3.0, Cl = 3.2. PYQ FREQUENCY: halogen reactivity-order in NEET, JEE-Main 1× per paper.

questions.stem: Common table salt (NaCl) is a compound of which two elements?
questions.explanation: TABLE SALT (NaCl, sodium chloride) — IONIC compound formed by Na⁺ + Cl⁻. SOURCES: (1) SEA SALT — evaporated from sea water (3.5% salinity). (2) ROCK SALT (HALITE) — mined from underground deposits (e.g., Khewra Salt Mine, Pakistan — world's 2nd largest). (3) BRINE WELLS. STRUCTURE: face-centered cubic crystal lattice; melting point 801°C. USES: (1) FOOD — preservation (osmotic pressure inhibits microbes), flavor, mineral. (2) INDUSTRIAL — chlor-alkali process (electrolysis of NaCl solution → NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂; both major industrial chemicals). (3) DE-ICING ROADS — lowers freezing point of water (winter use in temperate regions). (4) WATER SOFTENING — ion exchange with calcium. INDIA: GANDHI's DANDI MARCH (1930) — protested British SALT TAX; non-violent civil disobedience; iconic moment in independence movement. SODIUM CONTENT: human body needs ~1.5 g salt/day (~600 mg sodium); excess linked to hypertension. WHO recommends < 5 g/day. RICH-SALT FOODS: pickles, papads, snacks, cured meats. IODIZED SALT (with KI or KIO₃) — added since 1960s to prevent iodine deficiency (goiter); mandatory in India. PYQ FREQUENCY: chlorine compounds in NEET, NCERT-driven SSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: BLEACHING POWDER (chloride of lime) is chemically:
questions.explanation: BLEACHING POWDER — chemical formula: Ca(OCl)Cl or Ca(OCl)₂·CaCl₂·Ca(OH)₂ (a complex mix), commonly written CaOCl₂. The active species is the HYPOCHLORITE ion (OCl⁻) which oxidizes pigments → bleaching action. PREPARATION: Cl₂ + Ca(OH)₂ (slaked lime) → CaOCl₂ + H₂O. USES: (1) BLEACHING textiles (cotton, linen, paper). (2) WATER DISINFECTION — kills bacteria (~1-3 ppm chlorine in drinking water). (3) Disinfecting swimming pools, hospital floors, drains. (4) Chemical industry — producing other chlorine compounds. (5) Removing stains from clothes. ACTIVE CHLORINE CONTENT: ~30-35% available chlorine. WHY EFFECTIVE: when bleaching powder dissolves in water, it releases HOCl (hypochlorous acid) which is a powerful oxidizing agent. SAFETY: emits toxic Cl₂ gas if mixed with acids (NEVER mix bleach with toilet cleaners — risk of poisoning). HISTORICAL: developed by Charles Tennant (1799, Scotland) — sparked the textile bleaching revolution. ALSO see SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE (NaClO, household bleach 'Clorox') — solution form. INDIA — 'Chlorination' of municipal water is standard public-health practice. PYQ FREQUENCY: NCERT Class 10 staple — SSC, NEET 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which halogen is essential in our diet to prevent GOITER (thyroid swelling)?
questions.explanation: IODINE — essential micronutrient required for synthesis of THYROID HORMONES (T3 thyroxine, T4 triiodothyronine). DEFICIENCY: causes GOITER (enlarged thyroid gland), CRETINISM (severe in fetal development), hypothyroidism, learning disabilities. RDA: 150 µg/day for adults. SOURCES: iodized salt, sea-foods (fish, shrimp, seaweed), milk, eggs, dairy. INDIA — IODINE DEFICIENCY DISORDERS PROGRAMME (1962, renamed 1992): mandatory IODIZATION of all edible salt. India was among the first countries to mandate; sometimes briefly relaxed (2000-05) and then re-mandated. RESULT: goiter prevalence reduced from ~50% (1980s) to <5% in many areas. SALT-IODIZATION: KI (potassium iodide) or KIO₃ (potassium iodate) added at ~30 ppm. CHEMICAL FORMS of iodine: I₂ (purple-black solid), I⁻ (iodide ion in salts), IO₃⁻ (iodate), HI (hydroiodic acid). USES: (1) MEDICAL — Lugol's solution (iodine + KI in water) for wound disinfection; tincture of iodine. (2) DAVAVAN ('iodised salt') marketed widely in India. (3) RADIOLABEL — iodine-131 in thyroid imaging/treatment. EVENTS: WORLD IODINE DEFICIENCY DAY — 21 October. CHERNOBYL: I-131 release caused thyroid cancers; KI tablets distributed. PYQ FREQUENCY: iodine-thyroid in NEET, NCERT-driven SSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: When chlorine gas is bubbled through KBr solution, the reaction is:

options.option_text: No reaction occurs at room temp
Cl forms KClO₃ as the product
Br displaces Cl from KBr there

questions.explanation: DISPLACEMENT REACTION: a MORE REACTIVE halogen DISPLACES a LESS REACTIVE halogen from its salt. Reactivity: F > Cl > Br > I. So Cl₂ (more reactive) DISPLACES Br⁻ from KBr solution: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂. VISUAL: solution turns BROWNISH-RED (Br₂ liquid color); can be confirmed by adding hexane — Br₂ partitions into hexane (orange layer). SIMILAR: Cl₂ + KI → 2KCl + I₂ (forms purple iodine; hexane layer turns violet). ALSO: Br₂ + KI → 2KBr + I₂ (Br can displace I). REVERSE NOT POSSIBLE: I₂ + KCl ↛ no reaction (I is less reactive than Cl). CHEMISTRY PRINCIPLE: this is an OXIDATION-REDUCTION reaction. Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻ (Cl reduced); 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻ (Br oxidized). The HIGHER STANDARD ELECTRODE POTENTIAL species takes the electrons. KEY APPLICATION: extraction of bromine from sea water (Br⁻ in sea bittern is oxidized by Cl₂ to liberate Br₂); similarly iodine from sea-weed or brine. PYQ FREQUENCY: halogen displacement reactions in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT Class 10 — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: FLUORIDE in toothpaste helps prevent cavities by:
questions.explanation: FLUORIDE replaces hydroxyl ions in tooth enamel: HYDROXYAPATITE [Ca₅(PO₄)₃OH] → FLUOROAPATITE [Ca₅(PO₄)₃F]. Fluoroapatite is HARDER and MORE RESISTANT to ACID DECAY (caused by mouth bacteria fermenting sugars). DELIVERY: (1) FLUORIDATED WATER — ~0.7-1.0 ppm in many countries; widely debated due to skeletal fluorosis at higher doses. (2) FLUORIDE TOOTHPASTE — 1000-1500 ppm typical for adults. (3) Topical fluoride applications (dental clinics). (4) Fluoride mouth rinses. INDIA: water fluoridation NOT mandatory; some districts have natural fluoride > 1.5 mg/L causing FLUOROSIS — Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Rajasthan, Punjab particularly affected. FLUOROSIS — types: DENTAL FLUOROSIS (white/brown staining of teeth, irreversible cosmetic effect — not painful); SKELETAL FLUOROSIS (bone deformities, joint pain — long-term high exposure). MITIGATION: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Fluorosis (NPPCF, since 2008). FLUORIDE LIMIT: WHO permissible ≤ 1.5 mg/L. KEY CHEMISTRY: F⁻ small ion easily fits into apatite lattice; HF reactions with bone create stronger crystal structure. NOBEL: no specific Nobel; pioneered by H. T. Dean (USA, 1930s). PYQ FREQUENCY: fluoride health-effects in NEET, SSC GA, UPSC environment 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: AT ROOM TEMPERATURE, which halogen exists as a SOLID?
questions.explanation: STATES OF HALOGENS at room temperature (25°C, 1 atm): (1) FLUORINE (F₂) — pale yellow GAS, BP −188°C. (2) CHLORINE (Cl₂) — yellow-green GAS, BP −34°C. (3) BROMINE (Br₂) — red-brown LIQUID, BP 59°C; ONLY non-metal liquid at RT besides mercury. (4) IODINE (I₂) — purple-black SOLID, MP 114°C, BP 184°C. (5) ASTATINE (At) — radioactive, ultra-rare, predicted solid (though never isolated in bulk to confirm). TREND: as we go DOWN the group (F → I), MELTING and BOILING POINTS INCREASE. WHY: bigger molecules → stronger LONDON DISPERSION FORCES (van der Waals) holding them together. SUBLIMATION of IODINE: I₂ readily SUBLIMES (solid → gas without going through liquid) at slightly above room T — used to demonstrate sublimation in classroom; iodine vapor is purple-violet. USE: SUBLIMATION TEST is a way to PURIFY iodine (heat impure iodine, condense pure crystals on cold surface). DISCOVERY: chlorine by Scheele (1774); iodine by Courtois (1811, France) — discovered in seaweed ash; bromine by Balard (1826, France); fluorine by Moissan (1886, Nobel 1906). PYQ FREQUENCY: physical states of halogens in NEET, JEE-Main, SSC chemistry — 1× per cycle.
